newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Guatemala volcano alert ends as eruption subsides.
newsitem.headline: Guatemala volcano alert ends as eruption subsides.

text.p: Evacuated villagers returned home on Tuesday after a spectacular volcano eruption that spewed a two-mile (three km) high column of ash began to subside, emergency officials said.
"For the moment everything is quiet. There is no state of alert," Alvaro Herrera, spokesman for the National Emergency Committee, told Reuters.
Villagers had been evacuated from the slopes of the Pacaya volcano 24 miles (40 km) south of Guatemala City after a wave of eruptions on Monday that got stronger as the day wore on.
Fifty-three people were moved out but no one was injured in the blast, which was stronger than another one at the same volcano exactly one month earlier.

During the eruption, officials evacuated several dozen people from the village of El Caracol and placed other towns nearby on alert, said Colonel Oscar Guillermo Hernandez, head of the National Emergency Committee.
The 8,421-foot (2,552-meter) Pacaya is one of several active volcanos in Guatemala and it erupts regularly.

Just after midnight on Oct 11, the volcano erupted in its biggest explosion since 1987. A two-hour string of fiery explosions and molten lava flows were visible against the night sky from downtown Guatemala City. About 100 villagers were evacuated that night but no one was injured or killed.
